summary: The primary meaning of ذأب (dhAb) refers to the wolf, known for its predatory nature and cunning.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: He (a man, M) was frightened by the wolf; (M, K;) as also َئِبَ, aor. َأََ; and َؤُبَ, aor. َأَُ: (K:) or he (a man) was assailed, fallen upon, come upon, or overtaken, by the wolf. (Ibn-Buzurj, T.) And [hence, in the opinion of ISd, as he says in the M,] (tropical:) He was frightened by anything; (M, K;) and so, (AA, T, S, M, K,) inf. n. إِ ْآبٌ; (TA;) said of a man. (S.) [Hence also,] َأَبَهُ, (M, K,) aor. َأََ, (K,) [inf. n.
َأََّ see 1, last sentence but one. أّب الرَّحْلَ, (inf. n. تَ ْئِيبٌ, K,) He made, to the رحل [or camel's saddle ], what is termed a ِئْبَة, (M, K,) or ِئْب. (TA.) [See also مُ َأَّبٌ.]
أَ ْأَبَتِ الأَرْضُ (A, TA) The land abounded with wolves. (TA.) See also 1, in three places.
تَ َأََّ see 6, in two places: and see also 1, in three places.

ت آءب لِلنّاقَةِ (S, M, K) and لَهَا (M, K) (assumed tropical:) He disguised himself like a wolf to the she-camel, and, by so frightening her, made her to incline to, or affect, her young one: (S:) or he cloaked, or disguised, himself to the she-camel, making himself to seem like a wolf, in order to cause her to affect a young one that was not her own [ by moving her with pity by the supposed danger of the latter ]. (M, K) See also 1, in two places.
است أب النَّقَدُ The نقد [or ugly sheep ] became like wolves: a prov., applied to low, mean, or ignominious, persons, when they obtain ascendancy. (T, K.)
َأْبٌ (assumed tropical:) A large bucket with which one goes to and fro; thought by As to be from تَ َاؤُبُ الرِّيحِ: (M:) or in much [or quick ] motion, ascending and descending. (M, K.)

also pronounced ِيبٌ, without ء, (S, Msb, K,) originally with ء, (T, S,) The wolf, wild dog, or dog of the desert; كَلْبُ البَرِّ: (M, A, K:) applied to the male and the female; (Msb;) and sometimes, also, (Msb,) the female is called ِئْبَةٌ: (S, M, Msb, K:) pl. (of pauc., S, Msb) أَ ْؤُبٌ, and (of mult., S, Msb) ِئَابٌ, (S, M, Msb, K,) which may also be pronounced ِيَابٌ, with ى, because of the kesreh, (Msb,) and ُؤبَانٌ (S, M, Msb, K) and ِئْبَانٌ.

fem. of ِئْبٌ. (S, M, Msb, K.) Also (assumed tropical:) The [ angular ] intervening space between the دَفَّتَانِ [or two boards ] of the [ kinds of saddle called ] سَرْج and رَحْل (S, K, TA) and غَبِيط, (TA,) beneath the place of juncture of the two curved pieces of wood; (S;) [or] what is beneath the fore part of the place of juncture of the two curved pieces of wood (M, K) of the [ kinds of saddle called ] رَحْل and قَتَب and إِكَاف and the like; (M;) which falls, or lies, upon,…

a pl. of ِئبٌ. (TA.) Also, accord. to AA, (S,) The hair upon the neck and lip of the camel: (S, K;) and accord. to Fr, who says that it is a sing. [in this sense], (S,) the remains of the [ fur, or soft hair, called ] وَبَر [ after the greater part has fallen off or been shorn ]. (S, K. [See also ُوبَانٌ in art. وبْ, and ِيبَانٌ in art. يب.])

(also pronounced ُوَابَةٌ, T and K in art. وب,) A portion [or lock ] of hair, (S, A,) hanging down loosely from the middle of the head to the back: (A:) or the hair of the fore part of the head; the hair over the forehead; syn.
أَرْضٌ مَ ْأَبَةٌ A land containing, (S,) or abounding with, (M, K,) wolves: (S, M, K:) in the dial. of some of the tribe of Keys, مَ َيْبَةٌ, agreeing with ِيبٌ. (M.)

A boy having a ُؤَابَة. (T, S, A, K.) And (assumed tropical:) A [camel's saddle such as is called] غَبِيط [&c.] having [ a ُؤَابَة, i. e.] a skin, or piece of skin, hung upon its آخِرَة [or hinder part ]: (S:) or having a ِئْبَة [q. v.]. (TA.)

A man frightened by wolves: (A, TA:) or whose sheep, or goats, have been fallen upon by the wolf. (S, M, A, K.) [And hence,] (tropical:) Frightened [ as though by a wolf ]. (T, TA.) Also A horse, (Mgh,) or such as is called بِرْ َوْنٌ, (Lth, T, M, K,) and, accord. to the Tekmileh, an ass, and so مَ ْبُوبٌ, as though from ِيبَةٌ for ِئْبَةٌ, (Mgh,) Affected with the disease termed ِئْبَةٌ. (Lth, T, M, Mgh, K.)
(assumed tropical:) A man in a state of commotion, or fluctuation; from تَ َآءَبَتِ الرِّيحُ. (TA from a trad.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
